editorial:
Imagine stepping back in time to 1965 and hanging out with Walt Disney himself. You get to follow Julie Reems, the newly crowned Miss Disneyland Tencennial, as she starts her job as the park's official ambassador. The vibe is super positive and full of wonder, almost like you are getting a private VIP tour of the magic. You will see Walt acting as a proud father, showing off his dreams and the secret plans for the park's future. It feels less like a stiff documentary and more like a friendly chat about how a theme park grows.

What really makes this special is seeing the early blueprints and tiny models of famous rides like Pirates of the Caribbean and the Haunted Mansion before they were even built. It is a total treat for anyone who loves history or theme parks. While the pacing is a bit slow by today's standards, the nostalgia makes up for it.
endingExplained: The film wraps up with a bit of movie magic. Tinkerbell appears and uses her pixie dust to fly you away from the planning offices and straight into the heart of the park. You get to join Mickey Mouse and all his friends for a giant party. Everyone celebrates the 10th anniversary with music and cheering, ending the movie on a high note that makes you feel like part of the Disney family.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves Disney history and classic theme parks.
